previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with a one-day history of chills, fatigue, nausea, and watery diarrhea. Given his history of HCV cirrhosis, portopulmonary hypertension, and active liver transplant status, he was evaluated for possible infection. Workup included negative blood, urine, stool, and ascitic fluid cultures, with no evidence of bacterial infection or spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. A therapeutic paracentesis removed 3 liters of fluid, and imaging showed mild pulmonary edema likely due to decompensation from the viral illness. Empiric antibiotics were discontinued after 48 hours due to negative cultures, and diarrhea resolved with supportive care. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue home medications, use loperamide as needed, run tube feeds continuously, and monitor weight. Follow-up was arranged with his PCP and liver clinic.

INDICATION:  History of hepatitis C cirrhosis complicated by portal
hypertension, now with worsening diarrhea and low-grade fever, here to
evaluate for evidence of portal vein thrombosis.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen with contrast dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale, color and pulse wave Doppler ultrasound images of the
abdomen were obtained.

FINDINGS:  The liver demonstrates a diffusely coarsened echotexture with
nodular contours compatible with underlying cirrhosis.  No focal hepatic
lesion is identified.  No intrahepatic biliary dilation is seen.  The common
bile duct measures up to 11 mm in diameter in the free portion, which is not
significantly changed from the prior CT.  The patient is status post
cholecystectomy.  The spleen is massively enlarged, measuring 21 cm.  Small
volume ascites is seen along with multiple dilated collateral vessels in the
upper abdomen.

The pancreas is not visualized due to artifact from overlying bowel gas.  Both
kidneys are normal in size and position.  Both kidneys measure 12.3 cm in
length.  A simple-appearing cyst in the right kidney measures 2.7 x 2.4 x 2.1
cm, as seen on the prior CT.  No hydronephrosis, stones or solid masses are
identified in either kidney.

The main portal vein, right and left portal veins are patent with hepatopetal
flow and normal waveform.  Appropriate arterial waveforms are seen in the main
hepatic artery with a resistive index of 0.71.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Patent portal vein.
2.  Cirrhotic-appearing liver without focal hepatic lesion.
3.  Evidence of portal hypertension including massive splenomegaly, multiple
dilated upper abdominal collateral vessels, and ascites.
4.  2.7 cm simple right renal cyst.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of the patient with HCV cirrhosis and
portopulmonary hypertension.

___.

hilus most likely consistent with prior granulomatous exposure.  Bibasilar
opacities appear to be slightly more pronounced and may be consistent with

PROCEDURE:  Right internal jugular vein tunneled central venous catheter
removal.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:  The patient was brought to the angiography suite and
placed in the supine position.  The procedure was discussed with the patient. 
The right chest was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  The cuff
of the catheter was at the entrance site of the tunnel and gently removed. 
Subsequently, the entire catheter was removed and direct manual pressure was
held at the venotomy site and the tunnel site.  The tip of the line was cut
and sent for culture.  Pressure was held for 10 minutes.  There was no
evidence of bleeding after pressure was removed.  A sterile dressing was
applied.  The patient tolerated the procedure well without immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated removal of a right tunneled central venous
catheter.  The tip was sent for culture.  Culture is pending.

A left sided PICC line is coiled in the left subclavian vein.  A feeding tube
is seen in the stomach with its tip below the field of view.

An opacity at the right base could be dependent edema or a new pneumonia. The
cardiomediastinal silhouette and hilar contours are normal.  The pleural
surfaces are clear without effusion or pneumothorax.

PROCEDUREPROCEDURE DETAILS: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the
right basilic vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a
micropuncture set. Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and
immediately after establishing intravenous access. A peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire. The guidewire was then advanced into the superior
vena cava. A double lumen PIC line measuring 46 cm in length was then placed
through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the distal SVC under
fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest. The peel-away sheath and guidewire were
then removed. The catheter was secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile
dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS:

Right basilic vein approach double lumen PIC line with tip in the distal SVC.

IMPRESSION:

Successful placement of a 46 cm right basilic approach double lumen PIC line
with tip in the distal SVC.  The line is ready to use.

ascites.  The largest pocket within the left lower quadrant was targeted.  

PROCEDURE:

Ultrasound-guided diagnostic and therapeutic paracentesis.  

The procedure, risks, benefits and alternatives were discussed with the
patient and written informed consent was obtained.  

A preprocedure timeout was performed discussing the planned procedure,
confirming the patient's identity with three identifiers and reviewing a
checklist per ___ protocol.  

Under ultrasound guidance, an entrance site was selected in the left lower

The patient tolerated the procedure well without immediate complication. 
Estimated blood loss was minimal. 

Dr. ___ attending radiologist, was present for the critical portions of
the procedure.  

IMPRESSION:

Technically successful ultrasound-guided diagnostic and therapeutic
paracentesis.

If clinically indicated, please resubmit a new specimen after a 7 day or greater interval has elapsed.  Note, if there are compelling clinical reasons for repeat testing within a seven day window (see discussion in ___ laboratory manual), page the clinical microbiology resident on call (pager #___) to discuss the need for this repeat testing.

NO OVA AND PARASITES SEEN.  This test does not reliably detect Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora or Microsporidium. While most cases of Giardia are detected by routine O+P, the Giardia antigen test may enhance detection when organisms are rare.
